summary: The root نفق (nfq) primarily relates to something being in demand, selling well, or becoming brisk, like a market.
lane: 1 نَفَقَتِ السُّوقُ ذ The marked became brisk, its goods selling much; syn. قَامَت . (K.) -b2- نَفَقَ It was, or became, saleable; easy, or ready, of sale; or in much demand: see its syn. رَاجَ . -b3- نَفَقَتْ It (a commodity, سِلْعَة ,) was in much demand: and she (a woman) was demanded in marriage by many. (Msb.) -b4- نَفِقَتِ الدَّراَهِمُ , inf. n. نَفَقٌ , The dirhems passed away, came to an end, or became spent or exhausted; syn. نَفِدَت . (Msb.)

headwords.def: نَافَقَ He played the hypocrite in religion: (K, TA:) he pretended, to the Muslims, that he held the religion of El-Islám, concealing in his heart another religion than El-Islám. (Msb.) And نَافَقَ فُلاَنًا He acted with such a one hypocritically. (TK in art. دهن . [But I have not found this elsewhere.]) And نَافَقَ فِى المَحَبَّةِ [ He acted the hypocrite in respect of love ]. (Har, p. 505.) See خَانَ .
أَنْفَقَ He expended money: and he (God or a man) dispensed gifts.

headwords.def: تَنَفَّفَتِ الجَزُورُ [ The slaughtered camel became dealt out, or dispensed ]. (S, K in art. شيط .) تَنَفَّقَ : see Har, p. 472. تَنَفَّقَ It (a wound) cracked in its sides, and made, in the flesh, what resembled , i. e. holes in the ground, or subterranean excavations or habitations, pl. of نَفَقٌ . (TA in art. دسم .)

headwords.gloss: hole; holes in the ground; subterranean excavations

parts.t: of rats or mice. (S, TA in art.

headwords.def: نَفَقٌ : see سَرَبٌ أَنْفَاقٌ The hole of rats or mice. (S, TA in art. خفى :) see 1 in that art.: holes in the ground; or subterranean excavations or habitations; pl. of نَفَقٌ . (TA in art. دسم .) See 5. Also Fresh olive-oil: see فَاقٌ in art. فوق : also mentioned in art. نفق in the TA.

headwords.def: نَيْفَقٌ The part of a pair of drawers, or trousers, which is turned down at the top, and sewed, and through which the waistband, or string, passes. See نُقْبَة .
